title: Ensure that the default administrative credential file permissions are set to 600
description: Ensure that the admin.conf file (and super-admin.conf file, where it exists) have permissions of 600.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.1.13 Ensure that the default administrative credential file permissions are set to 600

audit.command:
set -f
ok=1; n=0
for f in /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf /etc/kubernetes/super-admin.conf; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue; n=$((n+1))
  p=$(stat -Lc %a "$f") || exit 1
  if [ $((0$p & 0177)) -ne 0 ]; then echo "noncompliant: $f mode $p"; ok=0; fi
done
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] || exit 1
if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: if [ -e /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf ]; then chmod u-x,go-rwx /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf; fi; if [ -e /etc/kubernetes/super-admin.conf ]; then chmod u-x,go-rwx /etc/kubernetes/super-admin.conf; fi

title: Ensure that anonymous requests to the API server are restricted
description: Disable anonymous requests to the API server entirely, or restrict anonymous authentication to only the specific endpoints that require it using the structured authentication configuration. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.2.1 Ensure that anonymous requests to the API server are restricted

audit.command: Determine which anonymous authentication mode is in use: # Check for structured authentication configuration AUTH_CONFIG=$(ps -ef | grep kube-apiserver | grep -oP '(?<=--authentication-config[= ])\S+') # Check for the --anonymous-auth flag ANON_AUTH=$(ps -ef | grep kube-apiserver | grep -oP '(?<=--anonymous-auth[= ])\S+') If --authentication-config is set Inspect the file for anonymous auth restrictions: cat "$AUTH_CONFIG" | grep -A 10 "anonymous:" Verify one of: • enabled: false — anonymous auth is fully disabled, or • enabled: true with a conditions list restricting access to only ...

remediation.command: Option 1 — Structured authentication configuration Add an anonymous section to the AuthenticationConfiguration file to restrict anonymous access to only required endpoints: apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 kind: AuthenticationConfiguration anonymous: enabled: true conditions: - path: /healthz - path: /livez - path: /readyz Start the API server with --authentication-config pointing to this file. Remove the --anonymous-auth flag if present. Option 2 — Disable anonymous authentication entirely: Edit the API server pod specification file ``/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` on the control plane node and set: --anonymous-auth=false Ensure load balancer health checks and any bootstrap processes authenticate to the API server.

title: Ensure that the --token-auth-file parameter is not set
description: Do not use token based authentication. Audited on control-plane nodes from the running process arguments (falls back to the kubeadm static pod manifest); SKIPs on nodes without that manifest.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.2.2 Ensure that the --token-auth-file parameter is not set

audit.command:
set -f
a=$(ps -eo args 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^([^ ]*/)?kube-apiserver( |$)' | head -n 1)
[ -n "$a" ] || a=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*"\{0,1\}\(--[^"]*\)"\{0,1\}[[:space:]]*$/\1/p' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -n "$a" ] || exit 1
g() { printf '%s\n' "$a" | awk -v k="--$1" '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){if($i==k&&i<NF)v=$(i+1); else if(index($i,k"=")==1)v=substr($i,length(k)+2)}} END{if(v!="")print v}'; }
has() { printf '%s\n' "$a" | awk -v k="--$1" '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i==k||index($i,k"=")==1) f=1} END{exit !f}'; }
ok=1
if has token-auth-file; then echo "noncompliant: --token-auth-file is set"; ok=0; fi
if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.command: Follow the documentation and configure alternate mechanisms for authentication. Then, edit the API server pod specification file /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml on the master node and remove the --token-auth-file=<filename> parameter.

title: Ensure that the --authorization-mode argument is not set to AlwaysAllow
description: Do not always authorize all requests. Audited on control-plane nodes from the running process arguments (falls back to the kubeadm static pod manifest); SKIPs on nodes without that manifest.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.2.6 Ensure that the --authorization-mode argument is not set to AlwaysAllow

remediation.guidance: Edit the API server pod specification file /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml on the Control Plane node and set the --authorization-mode parameter to values other than AlwaysAllow. One such example could be as below. --authorization-mode=RBAC

title: Ensure that the --anonymous-auth argument is set to false
description: Disable anonymous requests to the Kubelet server. Runs on each node: a kubelet command-line flag takes precedence over the config file named by --config (default /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml), otherwise the kubelet default applies.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.1 Ensure that the --anonymous-auth argument is set to false

remediation.guidance: If using a Kubelet config file, edit the file to set authentication: anonymous: enabled to false. If using executable arguments, edit the kubelet service file /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf on each worker node and set the below parameter in KUBELET_SYSTEM_PODS_ARGS variable. --anonymous-auth=false Based on your system, restart the kubelet service. For example: systemctl daemon-reload systemctl restart kubelet.service

title: Ensure that the --authorization-mode argument is not set to AlwaysAllow
description: Do not allow all requests. Enable explicit authorization. Runs on each node: a kubelet command-line flag takes precedence over the config file named by --config (default /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml), otherwise the kubelet default applies.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.2 Ensure that the --authorization-mode argument is not set to AlwaysAllow

remediation.command: If using a Kubelet config file, edit the file to set authorization: mode to Webhook. If using executable arguments, edit the kubelet service file /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf on each worker node and set the below parameter in KUBELET_AUTHZ_ARGS variable. --authorization-mode=Webhook Based on your system, restart the kubelet service. For example: systemctl daemon-reload systemctl restart kubelet.service

title: Ensure that the cluster-admin role is only used where required
description: The RBAC role cluster-admin provides wide-ranging powers over the environment and should be used only where and when needed. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.1 Ensure that the cluster-admin role is only used where required

audit.command: Obtain a list of the principals who have access to the cluster-admin role by reviewing the clusterrolebinding output for each role binding that has access to the cluster-admin role. kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,ROLE:.roleRef.name,SUBJECT:.subjects[*].name Review each principal listed and ensure that cluster-admin privilege is required for it.

remediation.command: Identify all clusterrolebindings to the cluster-admin role. Check if they are used and if they need this role or if they could use a role with fewer privileges. Where possible, first bind users to a lower privileged role and then remove the clusterrolebinding to the cluster-admin role : kubectl delete clusterrolebinding [name]

title: Avoid use of system:masters group
description: The special group system:masters should not be used to grant permissions to any user or service account, except where strictly necessary (e.g. bootstrapping access prior to RBAC being fully available) The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.7 Avoid use of system:masters group

audit.command: Review a list of all credentials which have access to the cluster and ensure that the group system:masters is not used.

remediation.command: Remove the system:masters group from all users in the cluster.

title: Minimize the admission of privileged containers
description: Do not generally permit containers to be run with the securityContext.privileged flag set to true. Requires kubectl with cluster-wide read access (KUBECONFIG); system namespaces are excluded and listed resources must be remediated or documented as exceptions. The benchmark marks this Manual; this audit automates its kubectl inventory step.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.2 Minimize the admission of privileged containers

audit.command:
out=$(kubectl get pods -A -o go-template='{{range .items}}{{$ns:=.metadata.namespace}}{{$p:=.metadata.name}}{{range .spec.containers}}{{$ns}} {{$p}} {{.name}} {{with .securityContext}}{{.privileged}}{{end}}{{"
"}}{{end}}{{range .spec.initContainers}}{{$ns}} {{$p}} {{.name}} {{with .securityContext}}{{.privileged}}{{end}}{{"
"}}{{end}}{{range .spec.ephemeralContainers}}{{$ns}} {{$p}} {{.name}} {{with .securityContext}}{{.privileged}}{{end}}{{"
"}}{{end}}{{end}}') || exit 1
bad=$(printf '%s
' "$out" | awk -v ex='^(kube-system|kube-public|kube-node-lease)$' 'NF && $1 !~ ex && ($4=="true")')
if [ -z "$bad" ]; then echo compliant; else printf '%s
' "$bad" | head -n 25; fi

remediation.command: Add policies to each namespace in the cluster which has user workloads to restrict the admission of privileged containers.

title: Ensure that the etcd data directory permissions are set to 700 or more restrictive
description: Ensure that the etcd data directory has permissions of 700 or more restrictive. Runs on etcd/control-plane nodes; the data directory comes from etcd --data-dir (default /var/lib/etcd).
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.1.11 Ensure that the etcd data directory permissions are set to 700 or more restrictive

audit.command:
set -f
a=$(ps -eo args 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^([^ ]*/)?etcd( |$)' | head -n 1)
[ -n "$a" ] || a=$(cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')
d=$(printf '%s\n' "$a" | tr ' "' '\n\n' | sed -n 's/^--data-dir=//p' | tail -n 1); d=${d:-/var/lib/etcd}
[ -d "$d" ] || exit 1
p=$(stat -Lc %a "$d") || exit 1
if [ $((0$p & 0077)) -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "noncompliant: $d mode $p"; fi

remediation.guidance: On the etcd server node, get the etcd data directory, passed as an argument --data-dir, from the below command: ps -ef | grep etcd Run the below command (based on the etcd data directory found above). For example, chmod 700 /var/lib/etcd

title: Client certificate authentication should not be used for users

reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.11 Minimize access to the approval sub-resource of certificatesigningrequests objects

audit.command: Review the users who have access to update the approval sub-resource of CertificateSigningRequests objects in the Kubernetes API.

remediation.command: Where possible, remove access to the approval sub-resource of CertificateSigningRequests objects.

reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.1.18 Ensure that the controller-manager.conf file ownership is set to root:root

audit.command:
set -f
f=""; for x in /etc/kubernetes/controller-manager.conf; do if [ -e "$x" ]; then f=$x; break; fi; done
[ -n "$f" ] || exit 1
o=$(stat -Lc %U:%G "$f") || exit 1
if [ "$o" = "root:root" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "noncompliant: $f $o"; fi

remediation.command: chown root:root /etc/kubernetes/controller-manager.conf

title: Ensure that the Kubernetes PKI directory and file ownership is set to root:root
description: Ensure that the Kubernetes PKI directory and file ownership is set to root:root. Runs on control-plane nodes; SKIPs where /etc/kubernetes/pki is absent.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.1.19 Ensure that the Kubernetes PKI directory and file ownership is set to root:root

audit.command:
out=$(find /etc/kubernetes/pki \( ! -user root -o ! -group root \) -print) || exit 1
if [ -z "$out" ]; then echo compliant; else printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25; fi

remediation.command: chown -R root:root /etc/kubernetes/pki/

title: Ensure that the admission control plugin AlwaysAdmit is not set
description: Do not allow all requests. Audited on control-plane nodes from the running process arguments (falls back to the kubeadm static pod manifest); SKIPs on nodes without that manifest.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.2.10 Ensure that the admission control plugin AlwaysAdmit is not set

audit.command:
set -f
a=$(ps -eo args 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^([^ ]*/)?kube-apiserver( |$)' | head -n 1)
[ -n "$a" ] || a=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*"\{0,1\}\(--[^"]*\)"\{0,1\}[[:space:]]*$/\1/p' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -n "$a" ] || exit 1
g() { printf '%s\n' "$a" | awk -v k="--$1" '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){if($i==k&&i<NF)v=$(i+1); else if(index($i,k"=")==1)v=substr($i,length(k)+2)}} END{if(v!="")print v}'; }
has() { printf '%s\n' "$a" | awk -v k="--$1" '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i==k||index($i,k"=")==1) f=1} END{exit !f}'; }
ok=1
v=$(g enable-admission-plugins); case ",$v," in *,AlwaysAdmit,*) echo "noncompliant: --enable-admission-plugins=$v includes AlwaysAdmit"; ok=0;; esac
if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit the API server pod specification file /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml on the Control Plane node and either remove the --enable-admission-plugins parameter, or set it to a value that does not include AlwaysAdmit.

reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.4.2 Ensure that the --bind-address argument is set to 127.0.0.1

remediation.guidance: Edit the Scheduler pod specification file /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml on the Control Plane node and ensure the correct value for the --bind-address parameter

title: Ensure that a unique Certificate Authority is used for etcd
description: Use a different certificate authority for etcd from the one used for Kubernetes. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 2.7 Ensure that a unique Certificate Authority is used for etcd

audit.command: Review the CA used by the etcd environment and ensure that it does not match the CA certificate file used for the management of the overall Kubernetes cluster. Run the following command on the master node: ps -ef | grep etcd Note the file referenced by the --trusted-ca-file argument. Run the following command on the master node: ps -ef | grep apiserver Verify that the file referenced by the --client-ca-file for apiserver is different from the --trusted-ca-file used by etcd.

remediation.command: Follow the etcd documentation and create a dedicated certificate authority setup for the etcd service. Then, edit the etcd pod specification file /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml on the master node and set the below parameter. --trusted-ca-file=</path/to/ca-file>

title: Service account token authentication should not be used for users
description: Kubernetes provides service account tokens which are intended for use by workloads running in the Kubernetes cluster, for authentication to the API server. These tokens are not designed for use by end-users and do not provide for features such as revocation or expiry, making them insecure. A newer version of the feature (Bound service account token volumes) does introduce expiry but still does not allow for specific revocation. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.1.2 Service account token authentication should not be used for users

audit.command: Review user access to the cluster and ensure that users are not making use of service account token authentication.

remediation.command: Alternative mechanisms provided by Kubernetes such as the use of OIDC should be implemented in place of service account tokens.

title: Bootstrap token authentication should not be used for users
description: Kubernetes provides bootstrap tokens which are intended for use by new nodes joining the cluster These tokens are not designed for use by end-users they are specifically designed for the purpose of bootstrapping new nodes and not for general authentication The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.1.3 Bootstrap token authentication should not be used for users

audit.command: Review user access to the cluster and ensure that users are not making use of bootstrap token authentication.

remediation.command: Alternative mechanisms provided by Kubernetes such as the use of OIDC should be implemented in place of bootstrap tokens.

title: Ensure that a minimal audit policy is created
description: Kubernetes can audit the details of requests made to the API server. The --audit-policy-file flag must be set for this logging to be enabled. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.2.1 Ensure that a minimal audit policy is created

audit.command: Run the following command on one of the cluster master nodes: ps -ef | grep kube-apiserver Verify that the --audit-policy-file is set. Review the contents of the file specified and ensure that it contains a valid audit policy.

remediation.command: Create an audit policy file for your cluster.

title: Ensure that the audit policy covers key security concerns
description: Ensure that the audit policy created for the cluster covers key security concerns. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 3.2.2 Ensure that the audit policy covers key security concerns

audit.command: Review the audit policy provided for the cluster and ensure that it covers at least the following areas :-• Access to Secrets managed by the cluster. Care should be taken to only log Metadata for requests to Secrets, ConfigMaps, and TokenReviews, in order to avoid the risk of logging sensitive data. • Modification of pod and deployment objects. • Use of pods/exec, pods/portforward, pods/proxy and services/proxy. • Use of the CertificateSigningRequest API which allows for creation of new credentials.

remediation.command: Consider modification of the audit policy in use on the cluster to include these items, at a minimum.

title: Ensure that the kubelet service file permissions are set to 600 or more restrictive
description: Ensure that the kubelet service file has permissions of 600 or more restrictive. Runs on each node; the path can be overridden with the kubelet_service_config environment variable (as in CIS-CAT).
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.1 Ensure that the kubelet service file permissions are set to 600 or more restrictive

audit.command:
set -f
f=""; for x in ${kubelet_service_config:-} /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf /usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/kubeadm.conf; do if [ -e "$x" ]; then f=$x; break; fi; done
[ -n "$f" ] || exit 1
p=$(stat -Lc %a "$f") || exit 1
if [ $((0$p & 0177)) -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "noncompliant: $f mode $p"; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the below command (based on the file location on your system) on the each worker node. For example, chmod 600 /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/kubeadm.conf

title: Ensure that the kubelet service file ownership is set to root:root
description: Ensure that the kubelet service file ownership is set to root:root. Runs on each node; the path can be overridden with the kubelet_service_config environment variable (as in CIS-CAT).
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.2 Ensure that the kubelet service file ownership is set to root:root

audit.command:
set -f
f=""; for x in ${kubelet_service_config:-} /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf /usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/kubeadm.conf; do if [ -e "$x" ]; then f=$x; break; fi; done
[ -n "$f" ] || exit 1
o=$(stat -Lc %U:%G "$f") || exit 1
if [ "$o" = "root:root" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "noncompliant: $f $o"; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the below command (based on the file location on your system) on the each worker node. For example, chown root:root /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/kubeadm.conf

title: If proxy kubeconfig file exists ensure permissions are set to 600 or more restrictive
description: If kube-proxy is running, and if it is using a file-based kubeconfig file, ensure that the proxy kubeconfig file has permissions of 600 or more restrictive. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.3 If proxy kubeconfig file exists ensure permissions are set to 600 or more restrictive

audit.command: Find the kubeconfig file being used by kube-proxy by running the following command: ps -ef | grep kube-proxy If kube-proxy is running, get the kubeconfig file location from the --kubeconfig parameter. To perform the audit: Run the below command (based on the file location on your system) on the each worker node. For example, stat -c %a <path><filename> Verify that a file is specified and it exists with permissions are 600 or more restrictive.

remediation.command: Run the below command (based on the file location on your system) on the each worker node. For example, chmod 600 <proxy kubeconfig file>

title: If proxy kubeconfig file exists ensure ownership is set to root:root
description: If kube-proxy is running, ensure that the file ownership of its kubeconfig file is set to root:root. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.4 If proxy kubeconfig file exists ensure ownership is set to root:root

audit.command: Find the kubeconfig file being used by kube-proxy by running the following command: ps -ef | grep kube-proxy If kube-proxy is running, get the kubeconfig file location from the --kubeconfig parameter. To perform the audit: Run the below command (based on the file location on your system) on the each worker node. For example, stat -c %U:%G <path><filename> Verify that the ownership is set to root:root.

remediation.command: Run the below command (based on the file location on your system) on the each worker node. For example, chown root:root <proxy kubeconfig file>

title: Ensure that the --kubeconfig kubelet.conf file permissions are set to 600 or more restrictive
description: Ensure that the kubelet.conf file has permissions of 600 or more restrictive. Runs on each node; the path can be overridden with the kubelet_config environment variable (as in CIS-CAT).
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.5 Ensure that the --kubeconfig kubelet.conf file permissions are set to 600 or more restrictive

audit.command:
set -f
f=""; for x in ${kubelet_config:-} /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf; do if [ -e "$x" ]; then f=$x; break; fi; done
[ -n "$f" ] || exit 1
p=$(stat -Lc %a "$f") || exit 1
if [ $((0$p & 0177)) -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "noncompliant: $f mode $p"; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the below command (based on the file location on your system) on the each worker node. For example, chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf

title: Ensure that the --kubeconfig kubelet.conf file ownership is set to root:root
description: Ensure that the kubelet.conf file ownership is set to root:root. Runs on each node; the path can be overridden with the kubelet_config environment variable (as in CIS-CAT).
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.6 Ensure that the --kubeconfig kubelet.conf file ownership is set to root:root

audit.command:
set -f
f=""; for x in ${kubelet_config:-} /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf; do if [ -e "$x" ]; then f=$x; break; fi; done
[ -n "$f" ] || exit 1
o=$(stat -Lc %U:%G "$f") || exit 1
if [ "$o" = "root:root" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "noncompliant: $f $o"; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the below command (based on the file location on your system) on the each worker node. For example, chown root:root /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf

title: If the kubelet config.yaml configuration file is being used validate permissions set to 600 or more restrictive
description: Ensure that if the kubelet refers to a configuration file with the --config argument, that file has permissions of 600 or more restrictive. Runs on each node; the path can be overridden with the kubelet_config_yaml environment variable (as in CIS-CAT).
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.9 If the kubelet config.yaml configuration file is being used validate permissions set to 600 or more restrictive

audit.command:
set -f
psarg() { ps -eo args 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^([^ ]*/)?$1( |\$)" | head -n 1 | awk -v k="--$2" '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){if($i==k&&i<NF)v=$(i+1); else if(index($i,k"=")==1)v=substr($i,length(k)+2)}} END{if(v!="")print v}'; }
p0=$(psarg kubelet config)
f=""; for x in ${kubelet_config_yaml:-} ${p0:-} /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml; do if [ -e "$x" ]; then f=$x; break; fi; done
[ -n "$f" ] || exit 1
p=$(stat -Lc %a "$f") || exit 1
if [ $((0$p & 0177)) -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "noncompliant: $f mode $p"; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command (using the config file location identified in the Audit step) chmod 600 /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml

title: If the kubelet config.yaml configuration file is being used validate file ownership is set to root:root
description: Ensure that if the kubelet refers to a configuration file with the --config argument, that file is owned by root:root. Runs on each node; the path can be overridden with the kubelet_config_yaml environment variable (as in CIS-CAT).
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.10 If the kubelet config.yaml configuration file is being used validate file ownership is set to root:root

audit.command:
set -f
psarg() { ps -eo args 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^([^ ]*/)?$1( |\$)" | head -n 1 | awk -v k="--$2" '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){if($i==k&&i<NF)v=$(i+1); else if(index($i,k"=")==1)v=substr($i,length(k)+2)}} END{if(v!="")print v}'; }
p0=$(psarg kubelet config)
f=""; for x in ${kubelet_config_yaml:-} ${p0:-} /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml; do if [ -e "$x" ]; then f=$x; break; fi; done
[ -n "$f" ] || exit 1
o=$(stat -Lc %U:%G "$f") || exit 1
if [ "$o" = "root:root" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "noncompliant: $f $o"; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command (using the config file location identied in the Audit step) chown root:root /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf

title: Ensure that the kubelet drop-in configuration directory and files have restrictive permissions
description: If the kubelet is configured with a drop-in configuration directory (--config-dir), ensure the directory and all .conf files within it have ownership set to root:root with permissions 755 for the directory and 644 for the files. Runs on each node; passes when the kubelet does not use --config-dir.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.1.11 Ensure that the kubelet drop-in configuration directory and files have restrictive permissions

audit.command:
set -f
psarg() { ps -eo args 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^([^ ]*/)?$1( |\$)" | head -n 1 | awk -v k="--$2" '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){if($i==k&&i<NF)v=$(i+1); else if(index($i,k"=")==1)v=substr($i,length(k)+2)}} END{if(v!="")print v}'; }
d=$(psarg kubelet config-dir)
if [ -z "$d" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi
[ -d "$d" ] || exit 1
ok=1
p=$(stat -Lc %a "$d") || exit 1; o=$(stat -Lc %U:%G "$d") || exit 1
if [ $((0$p & 0022)) -ne 0 ] || [ "$o" != root:root ]; then echo "noncompliant: $d $p $o"; ok=0; fi
for f in "$d"/*.conf; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  p=$(stat -Lc %a "$f") || exit 1; o=$(stat -Lc %U:%G "$f") || exit 1
  if [ $((0$p & 0133)) -ne 0 ] || [ "$o" != root:root ]; then echo "noncompliant: $f $p $o"; ok=0; fi
done
if [ "$ok" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: # Set directory permissions chown root:root /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d chmod 755 /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d # Set file permissions chown root:root /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/*.conf chmod 644 /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/*.conf

title: Ensure that the --streaming-connection-idle-timeout argument is not set to 0
description: Do not disable timeouts on streaming connections. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.5 Ensure that the --streaming-connection-idle-timeout argument is not set to 0

audit.command: Run the following command on each node: ps -ef | grep kubelet Verify that the --streaming-connection-idle-timeout argument is not set to 0. If the argument is not present, and there is a Kubelet config file specified by --config, check that it does not set streamingConnectionIdleTimeout to 0.

remediation.command: If using a Kubelet config file, edit the file to set streamingConnectionIdleTimeout to a value other than 0. If using command line arguments, edit the kubelet service file /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf on each worker node and set the below parameter in KUBELET_SYSTEM_PODS_ARGS variable. --streaming-connection-idle-timeout=5m Based on your system, restart the kubelet service. For example: systemctl daemon-reload systemctl restart kubelet.service

title: Ensure that the --make-iptables-util-chains argument is set to true
description: Allow Kubelet to manage iptables. Runs on each node: a kubelet command-line flag takes precedence over the config file named by --config (default /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml), otherwise the kubelet default applies.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.6 Ensure that the --make-iptables-util-chains argument is set to true

remediation.guidance: If using a Kubelet config file, edit the file to set makeIPTablesUtilChains: true. If using command line arguments, edit the kubelet service file /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf on each worker node and remove the --make-iptables-util-chains argument from the KUBELET_SYSTEM_PODS_ARGS variable. Based on your system, restart the kubelet service. For example: systemctl daemon-reload systemctl restart kubelet.service

title: Verify that the RotateKubeletServerCertificate argument is set to true
description: Enable kubelet server certificate rotation. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.11 Verify that the RotateKubeletServerCertificate argument is set to true

audit.command: Ignore this check if serverTLSBootstrap is true in the kubelet config file or if the --rotate-server-certificates parameter is set on kubelet Run the following command on each node: ps -ef | grep kubelet Verify that RotateKubeletServerCertificate argument exists and is set to true.

remediation.command: Edit the kubelet service file /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf on each worker node and set the below parameter in KUBELET_CERTIFICATE_ARGS variable. --feature-gates=RotateKubeletServerCertificate=true Based on your system, restart the kubelet service. For example: systemctl daemon-reload systemctl restart kubelet.service

title: Ensure that the Kubelet only makes use of Strong Cryptographic Ciphers
description: Ensure that the Kubelet is configured to only use strong cryptographic ciphers. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.12 Ensure that the Kubelet only makes use of Strong Cryptographic Ciphers

audit.command: The set of cryptographic ciphers currently considered secure is the following: • TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 • TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 • TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305 • TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 • TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305 • TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 Run the following command on each node: ps -ef | grep kubelet If the --tls-cipher-suites argument is present, ensure it only contains values included in this set.

remediation.command: If using a Kubelet config file, edit the file to set tlsCipherSuites: to TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_1 28_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305,TLS_ECDHE_R SA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305, TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 or to a subset of these values. If using executable arguments, edit the kubelet service file /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf on each worker node and set the --tls-cipher-suites parameter as follows, or to a subset of these values. --tls-cipher-suites=TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA25 6,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_ ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 Based on your system, restart the kubelet service.

title: Ensure that a limit is set on pod PIDs
description: Ensure that the Kubelet sets limits on the number of PIDs that can be created by pods running on the node. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.13 Ensure that a limit is set on pod PIDs

audit.command: Review the Kubelet's start-up parameters for the value of --pod-max-pids, and check the Kubelet configuration file for the PodPidsLimit . If neither of these values is set, then there is no limit in place.

remediation.command: Decide on an appropriate level for this parameter and set it, either via the --pod-max-pids command line parameter or the PodPidsLimit configuration file setting.

title: Ensure that the kube-proxy metrics service is bound to localhost
description: Do not bind the kube-proxy metrics port to non-loopback addresses. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.3.1 Ensure that the kube-proxy metrics service is bound to localhost

audit.command: review the start-up flags provided to kube proxy Run the following command on each node: ps -ef | grep -i kube-proxy Ensure that the --metrics-bind-address parameter is not set to a value other than 127.0.0.1. From the output of this command gather the location specified in the --config parameter. Review any file stored at that location and ensure that it does not specify a value other than 127.0.0.1 for metricsBindAddress.

remediation.command: Modify or remove any values which bind the metrics service to a non-localhost address

title: Minimize wildcard use in Roles and ClusterRoles
description: Kubernetes Roles and ClusterRoles provide access to resources based on sets of objects and actions that can be taken on those objects. It is possible to set either of these to be the wildcard "*" which matches all items. Use of wildcards is not optimal from a security perspective as it may allow for inadvertent access to be granted when new resources are added to the Kubernetes API either as CRDs or in later versions of the product. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.3 Minimize wildcard use in Roles and ClusterRoles

audit.command: Retrieve the roles defined across each namespaces in the cluster and review for wildcards kubectl get roles --all-namespaces -o yaml Retrieve the cluster roles defined in the cluster and review for wildcards kubectl get clusterroles -o yaml

remediation.command: Where possible replace any use of wildcards in ClusterRoles and Roles with specific objects or actions.

title: Minimize access to create pods
description: The ability to create pods in a namespace can provide a number of opportunities for privilege escalation, such as assigning privileged service accounts to these pods or mounting hostPaths with access to sensitive data (unless Pod Security Policies are implemented to restrict this access) As such, access to create new pods should be restricted to the smallest possible group of users. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.4 Minimize access to create pods

audit.command: Review the users who have create access to pod objects in the Kubernetes API.

remediation.command: Where possible, remove create access to pod objects in the cluster.

title: Minimize access to create persistent volumes
description: The ability to create persistent volumes in a cluster can provide an opportunity for privilege escalation, via the creation of hostPath volumes. As persistent volumes are not covered by Pod Security Admission, a user with access to create persistent volumes may be able to get access to sensitive files from the underlying host even where restrictive Pod Security Admission policies are in place. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.9 Minimize access to create persistent volumes

audit.command: Review the users who have create access to PersistentVolume objects in the Kubernetes API.

remediation.command: Where possible, remove create access to PersistentVolume objects in the cluster.

title: Ensure that access to the Kubelet API uses fine-grained subresources instead of nodes/proxy where possible
description: Where principals require access to specific Kubelet API endpoints such as /healthz, /pods, or /configz, use the fine-grained RBAC subresources nodes/healthz, nodes/pods, and nodes/configz instead of granting nodes/proxy access. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.1.14 Ensure that access to the Kubelet API uses fine-grained subresources instead of nodes/proxy where possible

audit.command: Review all ClusterRoleBindings and RoleBindings that grant access to the nodes/proxy subresource. For each principal identified, determine whether it requires access to /exec, /attach, /run, or /debug endpoints. If it does not, it should be using fine-grained subresources instead of nodes/proxy.

remediation.command: For each principal that does not require access to command execution endpoints, create a ClusterRole granting only the required fine-grained subresources.

title: Ensure that the cluster has at least one active policy control mechanism in place
description: Every Kubernetes cluster should have at least one policy control mechanism in place to enforce the other requirements in this section. This could be the in-built Pod Security Admission controller, or a third party policy control system. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.1 Ensure that the cluster has at least one active policy control mechanism in place

audit.command: Review the workloads deployed to the cluster to understand if Pod Security Admission or external admission control systems are in place.

remediation.command: Ensure that either Pod Security Admission or an external policy control system is in place for every namespace which contains user workloads.

title: Minimize the admission of root containers
description: Do not generally permit containers to be run as the root user. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.7 Minimize the admission of root containers

audit.command: List the policies in use for each namespace in the cluster, ensure that each policy either restricts the use of root containers by setting MustRunAsNonRoot or MustRunAs with the range of UIDs not including 0, or requires pods to set hostUsers: false to enable user namespaces.

remediation.command: Create a policy for each namespace in the cluster, ensuring that either MustRunAsNonRoot or MustRunAs with the range of UIDs not including 0, is set. Alternatively, require pods to set hostUsers: false to enable user namespaces. User namespaces require Linux kernel 6.3+ and a compatible container runtime (containerd 2.0+ or CRI-O 1.25+).

title: Minimize the admission of containers with the NET_RAW capability
description: Do not generally permit containers with the potentially dangerous NET_RAW capability. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.8 Minimize the admission of containers with the NET_RAW capability

audit.command: List the policies in use for each namespace in the cluster, ensure that at least one policy disallows the admission of containers with the NET_RAW capability.

remediation.command: Add policies to each namespace in the cluster which has user workloads to restrict the admission of containers with the NET_RAW capability.

title: Minimize the admission of containers with capabilities assigned
description: Do not generally permit containers with capabilities The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.9 Minimize the admission of containers with capabilities assigned

audit.command: List the policies in use for each namespace in the cluster, ensure that at least one policy requires that capabilities are dropped by all containers.

remediation.command: Review the use of capabilities in applications running on your cluster. Where a namespace contains applications which do not require any Linux capabilities to operate consider adding a policy which forbids the admission of containers which do not drop all capabilities.

title: Minimize the admission of Windows HostProcess Containers
description: Do not generally permit Windows containers to be run with the hostProcess flag set to true. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.10 Minimize the admission of Windows HostProcess Containers

audit.command: List the policies in use for each namespace in the cluster, ensure that each policy disallows the admission of hostProcess containers

remediation.command: Add policies to each namespace in the cluster which has user workloads to restrict the admission of hostProcess containers.

title: Minimize the admission of containers which have unmasked procmounts
description: Do not generally permit containers which require the use of unmasked proc mounts The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.2.13 Minimize the admission of containers which have unmasked procmounts

audit.command: List the policies in use for each namespace in the cluster, ensure that each policy disallows the admission of containers which have unmasked procMount sections.

remediation.command: Add policies to each namespace in the cluster which has user workloads to restrict the admission of containers which have unmasked procMount sections.

title: Ensure that the CNI in use supports Network Policies
description: There are a variety of CNI plugins available for Kubernetes. If the CNI in use does not support Network Policies it may not be possible to effectively restrict traffic in the cluster. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.3.1 Ensure that the CNI in use supports Network Policies

audit.command: Review the documentation of CNI plugin in use by the cluster, and confirm that it supports Ingress and Egress network policies.

title: Consider external secret storage
description: Consider the use of an external secrets storage and management system, instead of using Kubernetes Secrets directly, if you have more complex secret management needs. Ensure the solution requires authentication to access secrets, has auditing of access to and use of secrets, and encrypts secrets. Some solutions also make it easier to rotate secrets. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.4.2 Consider external secret storage

audit.command: Review your secrets management implementation.

remediation.command: Refer to the secrets management options offered by your cloud provider or a third-party secrets management solution.

title: Ensure that the --terminated-pod-gc-threshold argument is set as appropriate
description: Activate garbage collector on pod termination, as appropriate. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 1.3.1 Ensure that the --terminated-pod-gc-threshold argument is set as appropriate

audit.command: Run the following command on the Control Plane node: ps -ef | grep kube-controller-manager Verify that the --terminated-pod-gc-threshold argument is set as appropriate.

remediation.command: Edit the Controller Manager pod specification file /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml on the Control Plane node and set the --terminated-pod-gc-threshold to an appropriate threshold, for example: --terminated-pod-gc-threshold=10

title: Ensure that the --hostname-override argument is not set
description: Do not override node hostnames. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.7 Ensure that the --hostname-override argument is not set

audit.command: Run the following command on each node: ps -ef | grep kubelet Verify that --hostname-override argument does not exist. Note This setting is not configurable via the Kubelet config file.

remediation.command: Edit the kubelet service file /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf on each worker node and remove the --hostname-override argument from the KUBELET_SYSTEM_PODS_ARGS variable. Based on your system, restart the kubelet service. For example: systemctl daemon-reload systemctl restart kubelet.service

title: Ensure that the eventRecordQPS argument is set to a level which ensures appropriate event capture
description: Security relevant information should be captured. The eventRecordQPS on the Kubelet configuration can be used to limit the rate at which events are gathered and sets the maximum event creations per second. Setting this too low could result in relevant events not being logged, however the unlimited setting of 0 could result in a denial of service on the kubelet. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.8 Ensure that the eventRecordQPS argument is set to a level which ensures appropriate event capture

audit.command: Run the following command on each node: sudo grep "eventRecordQPS" /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf or If using command line arguments, kubelet service file is located /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubelet-args.conf sudo grep "eventRecordQPS" /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubelet-args.conf Review the value set for the argument and determine whether this has been set to an appropriate level for the cluster. If the argument does not exist, check that there is a Kubelet config file specified by --config and review the value in this location.

remediation.command: If using a Kubelet config file, edit the file to set eventRecordQPS: to an appropriate level. If using command line arguments, edit the kubelet service file /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf on each worker node and set the below parameter in KUBELET_ARGS variable. Based on your system, restart the kubelet service. For example: systemctl daemon-reload systemctl restart kubelet.service

title: Ensure that the --seccomp-default parameter is set to true
description: Ensure that the Kubelet enforces the use of the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 4.2.14 Ensure that the --seccomp-default parameter is set to true

audit.command: Review the Kubelet's start-up parameters for the value of --seccomp-default, and check the Kubelet configuration file for the seccompDefault . If neither of these values is set, then the seccomp profile is not in use.

remediation.command: Set the parameter, either via the --seccomp-default command line parameter or the seccompDefault configuration file setting.

title: Configure Image Provenance using ImagePolicyWebhook admission controller
description: Configure Image Provenance for your deployment. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.5.1 Configure Image Provenance using ImagePolicyWebhook admission controller

audit.command: Review the pod definitions in your cluster and verify that image provenance is configured as appropriate.

title: Create administrative boundaries between resources using namespaces
description: Use namespaces to isolate your Kubernetes objects. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.1 Create administrative boundaries between resources using namespaces

audit.command: Run the below command and review the namespaces created in the cluster. kubectl get namespaces Ensure that these namespaces are the ones you need and are adequately administered as per your requirements.

remediation.command: Follow the documentation and create namespaces for objects in your deployment as you need them.

title: Ensure that the seccomp profile is set to docker/default in your pod definitions

reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.2 Ensure that the seccomp profile is set to docker/default in your pod definitions

remediation.command: Use security context to enable the docker/default seccomp profile in your pod definitions. An example is as below: securityContext: seccompProfile: type: RuntimeDefault

reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.3 Apply Security Context to Your Pods and Containers

audit.command: Review the pod definitions in your cluster and verify that you have security contexts defined as appropriate.

remediation.command: Follow the Kubernetes documentation and apply security contexts to your pods. For a suggested list of security contexts, you may refer to the CIS Security Benchmark for Docker Containers.

title: The default namespace should not be used
description: Kubernetes provides a default namespace, where objects are placed if no namespace is specified for them. Placing objects in this namespace makes application of RBAC and other controls more difficult. Requires kubectl read access; fails when the default namespace holds objects other than the kubernetes Service, kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap and default ServiceAccount. The benchmark marks this Manual; this audit automates its kubectl inventory step.
reference: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.1.0 - 5.6.4 The default namespace should not be used

audit.command:
out=$(kubectl get pods,services,configmaps,secrets,serviceaccounts,deployments,statefulsets,daemonsets,jobs,cronjobs,ingresses,roles,rolebindings -n default -o name) || exit 1
bad=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -v '^$' | sed 's#^\([a-z]*\)\.[^/]*/#\1/#' | grep -Evx 'service/kubernetes|configmap/kube-root-ca\.crt|serviceaccount/default')
if [ -z "$bad" ]; then echo compliant; else printf '%s\n' "$bad" | head -n 25; fi

remediation.command: Ensure that namespaces are created to allow for appropriate segregation of Kubernetes resources and that all new resources are created in a specific namespace.
